A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Efficient Quadratic Corrections for Frank-Wolfe Algorithms. All 40 pages, including Appendices A–F, equations, eleven figures, and two tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original numerical experiments on regression, entanglement detection, projection problems, and tensor completion, including the additional analyses and performance profile in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original numerical experiments in Section 4 and Appendix F, including convergence plots, the 37-instance performance profile, and quadratic-correction success counts.

M1.justification: The stated pseudocode receives local input corrections. Algorithm 7 passes (S_t, x_t, a_t, s_t) instead of (S_t, a_t, s_t, v_t), and Algorithm 10's outer step uses current t-indexed states instead of uncomputed t+1 states. The overall CFW and quadratic-correction procedures are retained; these corrections do not establish implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain K-sparse regression, entanglement detection including noisy states, Birkhoff and shifted-ball projection/intersection scenarios, gisette logistic regression, and tensor completion. Appendix F's additional scenarios and 37-instance profile are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: FW, AFW, PFW, and BPCG; BCG in tensor completion; and AFW/BPCG inner-step comparisons for SOCGS. Appendix F.6 retains the same twelve baseline and quadratic-correction variants.

E3.justification: Appendix F.4 changes the reported SOCGS inner-step budget from k in {100, 200} to {50, 200}. This reconciles the appendix with Section 4.4 and Figure 4, which already specified {50, 200} in v3. It does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The active-set analyses, noisy-state tests, intersecting/disjoint ALM cases, SCG schedule comparison, post-PVM line-search experiment, and correction-success analyses are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix F.6 retains the same varying-parameter/seed instance collection and shifted-geometric-mean summaries. There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 1–11 retain identical plotted content, and Tables 1–2 retain all numerical entries. For example, the entanglement BPCG-LP entry remains 2/473 and BPCG-MNP remains 596/889. The reported empirical rankings and findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 8 replaces its general convex L-smooth assumption with an explicit convex quadratic objective and specifies Algorithms 4, 5, and 8, aligning the statement with its construction and proof. Lemma 13 broadens S from vertices to feasible points, and Theorem 4's proof adds the continuity/compactness argument for convergence to the minimizer set. The principal convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction now describes SCG's O(1/sqrt(t)) rate as matching a nonsmooth complexity bound, replacing the comparison to an original FW method. The main CFW, quadratic-correction, SOCGS, and computational-speedup contributions otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: The significance of the SCG rate is reinterpreted relative to problem complexity rather than an existing FW rate. The empirical mechanism explanations and limitations concerning QC-LP infeasibility, numerical precision, correction overhead, and SOCGS stopping conditions remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The corrected inner-step budget in Appendix F.4 removes a reproducibility inconsistency. Other implementation disclosures—including FrankWolfe.jl, hardware, secant line search, correction schedules, and Hessian construction/storage—are retained, with no changed code or data access information.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yudin's Problem complexity and method efficiency in optimization (1983) to support the revised positioning of the SCG convergence rate. The remaining cited works and relationships to existing FW, SCG, and SOCGS methods are retained.

P1.justification: Copyediting improves grammar and sentence flow, standardizes algorithm names, introduces CS/LPS/FCS labels, and updates funding acknowledgments. These are local editorial refinements; section ordering and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Minor caption edits, relabeled algorithm boxes, numbered conditions in Algorithm 2, and local page reflow alter presentation. Figures and tables retain their designs, axes, legends, and placement; no experimental display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 improves internal consistency by making Theorem 8's quadratic setting and required QC-MNP variant explicit, correcting pseudocode inputs, and reconciling Appendix F.4's inner-step budget with Figure 4. Copyediting also improves readability. The narrower theorem statement better matches the existing construction and proof. With the empirical evidence and principal convergence results retained, these gains support a limited overall improvement.
